articles.title: Meet Trilorah: prepare the service, follow the sermon
articles.audience: Church volunteers, worship leaders, and church leaders evaluating Trilorah
articles.question: What does Trilorah do, and where should our team begin?
articles.information_gain: A compact introduction connected to a runnable volunteer rehearsal, with the current operator-press boundary stated before recognition claims.
articles.evidence: LiveBody and LibraryTabs establish the current workspace. RunRail supplies the service structure. VerseDelivery.promote accepts explicit operator/remote sources only.

visuals.shot: Operator workspace with a short synthetic run, library tabs, preview, and live all visible. Add four small labels; keep their UI names unchanged.
visuals.alt_text: Trilorah operator workspace showing a service run, content libraries, preview, and live output.

visuals.shot: Optional 20–35 second captioned clip of one real spoken reference appearing as a candidate, followed by a deliberate operator send. Label the recording as a demonstration.
visuals.alt_text: A spoken reference becomes a suggestion before the operator sends it live.

articles.release_check: Walk the four-item sample service in the release desktop build. Confirm the current tab labels and explicit publication behavior. Do not use the website example assistant as proof of desktop capability.

articles.title: Your first service in Trilorah: a rehearsal checklist
articles.audience: A volunteer preparing to operate Trilorah for the first time
articles.question: What should I check before using Trilorah in a service?
articles.information_gain: A single rehearsal checklist that separates screen delivery, sound capture, transcription, and file saving instead of treating button states as success.
articles.evidence: OutputsTile maps roles/displays; MicPicker selects audio; Stage/ScripturesBrowser distinguish preview and direct-send actions; TriPackageActions requires an initial file save for autosave.

visuals.shot: Dashboard Outputs with a real connected rehearsal display and its job/display controls. Use a generic device label where possible.
visuals.alt_text: Output job and display choices in Trilorah.

visuals.shot: Operator workspace during a prepared four-item practice service. Use the article checklist beside the image rather than a screenshot of a checklist.
visuals.alt_text: A practice service containing a welcome, song, scripture, and closing slide.

articles.release_check: Rehearse on actual hardware. Verify clear/restore and initial save. The practice sermon is not an isolated output sandbox; all sample live actions belong in rehearsal.

articles.title: Connect a microphone to Trilorah and check that it hears you
articles.audience: An operator setting up sermon listening
articles.question: How do I select the right microphone and confirm that transcription works?
articles.information_gain: A two-part success check using both fresh sound and fresh words, plus the distinction between pairing a phone and using it as audio.
articles.evidence: MicPicker.choose persists input and can restart listening. openMicrophone handles permissions/devices. PhoneMicPanel connects separately from use phone audio. The engine listen path updates UI before all backend work completes.

visuals.shot: Open Audio beneath preview with the intended device selected; mask personal device names if necessary.
visuals.alt_text: The Audio menu with a microphone selected.

visuals.shot: A single cropped view containing the responding audio level and fresh sample transcript from the same sentence. Optionally record this check with captions.
visuals.alt_text: Audio activity and new transcript words during a microphone check.

articles.release_check: Run a real input and transcription test; if showing phone steps, pair a test phone and verify use phone audio separately. Exclude live pairing codes from the published image. No engine-key provisioning tutorial is asserted.

articles.title: How Trilorah recognizes scripture during a sermon
articles.audience: Operators and church leaders evaluating sermon recognition
articles.question: How do spoken references and quotations become scripture suggestions, and who controls projection?
articles.information_gain: A source-backed explanation distinguishing explicit references, quotation evidence, display translation, and the non-optional live operator action.
articles.evidence: main.ts stages detections with manualOnly and rejects auto-mode-set enabled. VerseDelivery.promote blocks automatic sources. QuoteMatcher.loadIndex reports KJV/BSB wordings. ScriptureCatches exposes recent and typed search with live result selection.

visuals.shot: A real captured reference with the transcript clue and candidate reference visible. Caption the example and tested Bible translation.
visuals.alt_text: A spoken Bible reference and its suggested passage in Trilorah.

visuals.shot: Two frames from the same test: candidate in preview, then the chosen verse live after the operator press. A short captioned clip is preferable if available.
visuals.alt_text: The operator checks the candidate before sending the verse live.

articles.release_check: Record explicit-reference and quotation examples on the release build. If a quotation example does not match, show the failure/fallback or choose a verified example; do not fake the UI. Reconfirm auto-mode prohibition before publishing.

articles.title: Put the right content on the right screen in Trilorah
articles.audience: Operators setting up a projector, stage display, stream, or timer
articles.question: How do I assign an output to a connected display and verify it?
articles.information_gain: A destination-first tutorial with a physical confirmation step and the current distinction between dashboard assignment and settings preferences.
articles.evidence: OutputsTile.rowsFor provides job/display handlers; fromEngine.saveRole/saveDisplay persists choices. ROLE_SHOWS describes projector/stream/stage/timer. Settings exposes layout preferences rather than the effective display assignment workflow.

visuals.shot: Expanded Dashboard Outputs showing actual connected hardware, job selector, display selector, and status.
visuals.alt_text: A projector output assigned to a connected display.

visuals.shot: Photo of a real rehearsal screen showing an original Projector check slide; exclude people unless appropriately arranged.
visuals.alt_text: The test slide on the physical display used for the service.

articles.release_check: Test screen assignments and no-screen/off on real hardware. Never substitute design.html sample screens. A stream role does not prove an external broadcast is configured.

articles.title: Build an order of service your next volunteer can follow
articles.audience: Service planners and volunteer presentation operators
articles.question: How do I organize segments, content, and notes for a service?
articles.information_gain: An actual handoff-ready run with content and timing notes, including the difference between a label, an operator note, and presentable material.
articles.evidence: RunHeaderActions onArrange adds segments and loadDefault replaces the run. RunRail/useRun provide segment edits and notes. Library drag payloads carry content; a queued song label alone is insufficient for live text.

articles.title: Prepare song lyrics that are easy to follow on Sunday

articles.information_gain: An end-to-end saved-song check and precise preview/send distinction, rather than stopping at the lyric-entry form.
articles.evidence: SongEditor organizes sections and saves. SongLyricsEntry provides input. AddSongDialog opens online material into an editor. SongSheet separates Preview section and go live.

articles.title: Add images and videos to Trilorah without confusing media and backgrounds
articles.audience: Operators preparing visuals for worship, sermons, and announcements
articles.question: How do I import media, find online visuals, and decide how they should appear?
articles.information_gain: One image shown in two distinct jobs, with concrete download completion and the live-changing background interactions explained.
articles.evidence: MediaBrowser.addHere imports and stages media. StockSearch.pick awaits download before onPick. Theme clicks stage backgrounds; double-click/live drops change live backgrounds. Online tab stages standalone media.

articles.release_check: Test local import, download, provider failure state, and media playback in the release build. Credential setup is evolving in parallel: update only after the parent verifies the working path. Do not promise all remote links are offline files.

articles.title: Find a Bible passage when you remember the words, not the reference
articles.audience: Operators following a sermon or preparing a scripture reading
articles.question: How can I search by a phrase, person, event, or recent speech?
articles.target_query: find Bible passage by phrase Trilorah
articles.information_gain: A decision between three search paths that documents the different publication behavior of reference rows and phrase-result cards.
articles.evidence: ScriptureStorySearch corrects typos and offers use original; ScriptureFindOverlay card selection pushesReference. ScripturesBrowser reference submit sends live. find-heard-scripture limits recent words, supplies meaning availability, and reads actual passage text.

articles.release_check: Run each example in the intended translation; avoid implying a guaranteed top match. Verify typo reversal and unavailable meaning behavior. Recent speech is limited; no whole-sermon search claim.

articles.title: Save a Trilorah service and move it to another computer

articles.evidence: TriPackageActions savePackage, prepareSave, inspect, and autosave effect implement selection, initial save, warnings, export and replacement consent. triClient applies selected resources and renderer state.

articles.title: Make scripture and lyrics readable from the back of the room
articles.audience: Volunteers choosing text styles and backgrounds
articles.question: Which Trilorah controls help projected words remain clear in the actual room?
articles.information_gain: A reproducible Trilorah adjustment example coupled with a physical viewing-distance check, with no universal pixel-size prescription.
articles.evidence: ThemesEditor exposes font/sizes/shadow/dimness/blur/position/margins/width. Most layout changes stage in preview; transition handlers differ. Background interactions distinguish preview/live. SongEditor splits dense lyric sections.

articles.evidence: Capture paths emit input/permission failures; selected device can differ from connected phone. Notices route to controls. Practice sermon emits recognizer text and does not test actual microphone/ASR capture.

articles.title: Teach a new Trilorah volunteer one complete service

articles.evidence: The operator surface supplies the practiced tasks. ProductGuide and registered walkthroughs supply Show me / I’ll do it and bounded cursor guidance. Guide workflow coverage is changing in this implementation task.

articles.title: Use a preacher sound check and review missed scripture
articles.audience: Operators improving recognition with a regular preacher
articles.question: How do sound checks, corrections, and teaching help without promising perfect recognition?
articles.target_query: Trilorah preacher sound check recognition review
articles.information_gain: A specific feedback loop that distinguishes verified answers from unreviewed examples and separates aliases, vocabulary, and ignored tails.
articles.evidence: ProfileView selects today’s preacher. LearningActions provides local sound checks, verified review answers, corrections and missed examples. Teaching separates alias/vocabulary/ignored-tail stages. main rejects automatic projection regardless of readiness.

articles.release_check: Test sound-check model setup and one saved correction. Confirm local test/provider distinction. Do not claim acoustic voice cloning, perfect learning, or automatic projection when a score rises.

articles.title: Turn a service programme into a run you can rehearse
articles.audience: Volunteers receiving the service plan as a message, flyer, or image
articles.question: How do I scan or paste a programme, review it, and finish the service preparation?
articles.target_query: import church programme Trilorah order service
articles.information_gain: A transparent programme-to-rehearsal example that includes human review and the current append-versus-schedule-replacement behavior.
articles.evidence: RunHeaderActions.scan returns rows to review and falls back to text with explanatory errors. onAdd appends run.addSegments but replaces the engine schedule through setServiceSchedule. ScanReview edits proposed rows before adding.
